_comment: Pinned, hashed manifest for the differential CPU oracle (ADR 0001). Fixtures are FETCHED, NOT VENDORED: only this small file is committed; the vectors land in the gitignored build/cpuoracle/ cache via tests/cpuoracle/fetch_vectors.py. Each core pins an immutable upstream ref (tag or commit), the SHA-256 of the fetched .tar.gz source archive, and a mirrors[] list (primary + >=1 fallback) of byte-identical URLs for that archive. Bump a pin deliberately: re-fetch, recompute sha256, update ref + expected_file_count.

provenance.note: Independently derived (not MAME-generated); strict state + cycle equality is meaningful and required. This corpus caught two real MAME z80 WZ/MEMPTR bugs (now fixed).

Independently derived (not MAME-generated); strict state + cycle equality is meaningful and required. Three unstable/illegal opcodes (8b ANE, ab LXA, bb LAS) surfaced as MAME-vs-corpus findings; 12 JAM opcodes never retire. Evidence-based skip list lives in cpuoracle.cpp.

provenance.upstream_status: Generated using the microcoded core in MAME; any bugs that exist in MAME's microcoded M68000 emulator will exist here too. All tests except TAS and TRAPV are verified as good. TAS doesn't properly handle the special 5-cycle TAS read-modify-write timing; TRAPV appears to trigger incorrectly based on the S bit. Address-error cases carry re/we cycle types where AS isn't asserted and results aren't committed.
provenance.authority: ADR 0006: the in-tree interpreter (-drc 0), NOT this corpus, is the m68000 behavioral authority. The corpus is a conformance probe. This is a deliberate asymmetry from z80/m6502 (which are independent), justified by provenance.

cycle_divergence_allowlist.case_level: any case with the fetcher's addr_error marker (re/we address-error transaction)
cycle_divergence_allowlist.rationale: TAS/TRAPV are upstream-STATUS-flagged corpus-generation issues; address-error cases don't commit a comparable cycle count. State is asserted for all of these; only the cycle comparison is exempt (ADR 0006 Leg A).
